LESSON: READING 10.2.2 COMPREHENSION

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade two
Subject: General
Strand: Strand 10
Topic 10.2: Reading 10.2.2 Comprehension
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Reading 10.2.2 Comprehension, part of Strand 10 in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade two General.

Key inquiry question: What do you think will happen in this story? 2. What do the pictures tell us about the story?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Reading 10.2.2 Comprehension together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Critical thinking and problem solving: is enhanced as the learner interacts with the text to answer indirect comprehension questions.

• Creativity and imagination: is enhanced as the learner creates mental pictures of events, characters and places in a text.

Values:
Respect: is enhanced as the learner exercises patience with others as they talk about their own experiences in relation to the story.

Link to

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
Life skills (effective communication) is enhanced as the learner retells the story in their own words.

Link to other Learning Areas:

Comprehension is essential in all learning areas.

Suggested Learning Resources:

Digital texts, assistive technology such as universal cuffs/wrist braces/arm braces, weighted pencil/pen grips, page-turners, adapted digital devices

Other Related Service Providers: Resource person, speech therapist, Learner support assistance, Occupational Therapist, Physiotherapist
